column3: “I will relent on the good” is rendered “think better of the good,” and “said” as “promised.”
The Hebrew is difficult (“strange waters”); NASB has “water from a foreign land.” The meaning is uncertain.
NASB follows a reading “I will show them My back”; the Hebrew vowels read “I will look at them.”
NASB supplies “Surely”; “word” is rendered “the divine word.”
“The voice of my opponents” is rendered “what my opponents are saying.”
“Pour them over the hands of the sword” is rendered “deliver them up to the power of the sword.”
